newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up on economy, baht pares gains.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up on economy, baht pares gains.

text.p: Thai stocks rose on Thursday in response to positive economic data but concerns surrounding the baht's continued slide against the dollar pared gains, analysts said.
The SET index closed up 5.79 points, or 0.71 percent, to 820.18. The SET 50 added 0.66 points, or 1.09 percent to 61.39. Turnover was 3.94 billion baht.

"These were pretty good numbers .. but the baht had a slightly dicey day, it slid to 26 against the dollar at one stage and that's slightly worrying," said Richard Henderson, head of research at Krungthai Thanakit.

Traders said a 0.70 percent gain in response to a sharp fall in November's current account deficit ran out of steam as the baht came under attack offshore and investors appeared to ponder the economic figures.
"These are very good numbers but the market appears to be obsessed with the export data and may be a little upset by the year on year manufacturing figures," Henderson said.

The export figures showed a year on year decline as did manufacturing output data. "It's a market that likes to be told what is good and what's bad and it takes a couple of days to digest this kind of thing," he said.
Though volume was small foreigners were thought to have been net buyers, traders said.
The telecommunications and energy sector both advanced with TelecomAsia adding 1.25 baht to 50.50 and Advanced Info, heavily sold on Wednesday, picked up four to 250.
After a see-saw day Finance One gained 0.25 baht to 37.25 after falling to 34.50 early. The stock topped the active list.
The market was expected to gain early on Friday as investors digested the economic data. The numbers should boost sentiment in the equity market and help calm baht nerves, analysts said.
